goal.en: Place the heads of Ghash and Urgash on the altar and return to Alexey Borodin.

startText.en:
Vengeance! That is what I seek!
My companions' deaths must be avenged. Those scaly beasts must cower and flee when they hear someone mention the demon hunters. Or maybe we should call ourselves draconid hunters, eh?
I know how to sow horror in the hearts of those loathsome traitors. The kind of horror they've never experienced. But since I'm wounded, you shall be the instrument of my vengeance!
I saw an altar here on the island where the draconids offer sacrifices to their deity. They call this thing "Fiery Father." Ha! We'll see how it will like the heads of its own offspring put on the altar!
Ghash, the drake chieftain, and Urgash, the draconid leader... Their heads on the altar shall be stuff of nightmares for those who killed my friends!

checkText.en: The souls of my fallen comrades long for revenge. What can be more frightening than true death?

finishText.en:
I heard the desperate screams and dying wheezing of the winged beasts. Well done, comrade.
The drakes shall remember this day as one of just retribution. And that's what all traitors should expect!

checkText.en: We should have exterminated all those beasts while we were at the Dragon Ring...

finishText.en:
Yes! His dying roar made even cliffs shake. And the surviving drakes were darting around the sky like headless chickens.
It was an unforgettable sight!

goal.en: Kill Ghash, the drake chieftain, and bring his head to Alexey Borodin.

startText.en:
Remember Ghash, the drake chieftain? The one you were sparring with?
It's time to prove you're equally proficient in real combat. Remember where to find him? Well, I'll remind you. Ghash dwells in the mountains to the east of here.
Destroy him! With their chieftain dead, the drakes will start to quarrel, and we'll add some fuel to the fire. I have an idea... Chop his head off and bring it to me. I'll find a suitable application for that brainless skull.

checkText.en: Oh... My wounds are getting worse. But I won't die until my friends are avenged!

finishText.en: I can see their cold blood on your hands... No need to say anything. My comrades would have been grateful.

goal.en: Kill 3 mature draconid sorcerers and 3 wise draconid healers and return to Alexey Borodin.

startText.en:
I don't know exactly who took part in the raid on our camp. All draconids look the same to me. But that doesn't mean we'll refrain from revenge!
Go to their village and kill as many draconids as you can. If we can't take revenge on the actual killers, we'll take revenge on their entire race. Blood for blood, death for death! I'm not interested in regular warriors, they're just an instrument. It's those damn priests and sorcerers that I want! They've turned the draconids against us. Them and their terrible god...
Please destroy them! Help me exact vengeance!
If anyone is to be punished, it's the strongest and most experienced draconids. If the elimination of our squad was planned, it is those bastards who are the culprits.

checkText.en: I look forward to my wounds healing, so that I can wield a blade to avenge my fallen friends.

finishText.en:
Is Urgash dead? Praised be the gods! I fear to imagine how much grief that (literally!) cold-blooded traitor could have brought to our kind.
His head will make a perfect decoration for the draconids' altar. Let them tremble, for the hand of retribution shall strike them all!

goal.en: Kill Urgash, the draconid chieftain, and bring his head to Alexey Borodin.

startText.en:
Urgash, that goddamn hypocrite bastard! He smiled, assuring me of our eternal friendship, called me friend and brother... But once I turned my back, he shoved his blade into it!
Herein lies a sorrowful lesson... You can trust no one! We were wrong about the draconids' loyalty. That misconception cost my comrades-in-arms their lives.
An eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth. Urgash must die! That traitor deserves no mercy.
Unfortunately, my wounds won't let me revel in his last breath. Therefore, bring me his head! I want to look into his glazed-over eyes!

checkText.en: The draconids' deaths bring me joy. That'll teach them how to steal our eggs!

finishText.en:
Five fangs and five claws... Excellent!
Now we believe that you are, like us, a true enemy of the draconids. We're ready to forgive you for your past misdeeds.

goal.en: Bring 5 drake claws and 5 draconid fangs to Slark-Slark at the dockside of Draconid Island.

startText.en:
Halt! We don't wish to fight. We wish to speak.
You used to help our enemies. Now you're fighting them. The enemy of our enemy can be our friend. If you help us, we are willing to forgive you.
But first you have to prove you truly are an enemy to the draconids. Bring me five drake claws and five draconid fangs. Then we'll be able to trust you.

checkText.en: Eggs... Our eggs... Our offspring... Oh, how I've missed them.

finishText.en:
Stranger, I can't believe my eyes. You've made it!
Now the draconids may fly off the handle because they won't be able to steal our kids again.
Thank you, stranger. Please accept this reward as a token of my gratitude for what you've done.

startText.en:
Listen to what I've got to say.
You can make amends for the evil your race has done to ours. And bring plenty of sorrow to those blasted draconids along the way.
I'm talking about the eggs. Those stolen from our village. Get them back! We want our kids back! As for the draconids, let them all die out without any offspring.
And remember: grab only those eggs that are still ours. Those that now belong to the draconids should be broken, if possible.
That's it. Now go. We'll be waiting for you.

finishText.en: Freeze! Move and I'll shoot you dead! Who are you? Answer quickly!

goal.en: Go to Draconid Island and locate saboteur Roman Lazeykin.

startText.en:
I hope you've got no pressing matters to attend to? I've been waiting too long for someone I can entrust this important mission to. Listen carefully, as there's very little time left.
The treacherous draconids have gone ahead to a small allod we call the Frontier. Some of the draconids remained on the Island, however, posing a serious threat to the Citadel.
I've sent a couple of scouts there, those who are obedient to the Master's Will. Plenty of time has passed and I still haven't heard from them.
Please go to Draconid Island and find Roman Lazeykin. Find out what he was able to learn, and then proceed as you see fit. We must eliminate the threat posed by the draconids as soon as possible!
When you're ready, go talk to the Master's Voice. It will help you teleport to the Island.

checkText.en: Hey, we're here! Let us out!

finishText.en: Oh...Thanks a lot! We thought we were goners for sure, soon to be devoured by that scaly filth!

goal.en: Free the Rowdy Family.

startText.en:
So that's how it is... Those pompous Sentinels finally remembered that we exist!
You want to know where my partner is? Caught by the draconids, that's where! Now they're rotting away in a cage.
Why "they"? Because my partners are gibberlings! The Rowdy Family! Rowdy they are, no doubt... When the draconids attacked us, they charged right into the scuffle. Got captured and thrown into a guarded cage. Now what can I do, all alone? I don't even know how to help them. I feel sorry for them - they're like little kids who don't know any better.
Look, help me, will you? You know about the rule in the Imperial army, "Help a comrade in need, even if it means your end"!
So here's the situation: the cage is to the east, and there's only one guard who keeps the key on him all the time. No one else. Whack the guard, free those silly fuzzies and bolt!

checkText.en: I can't believe my eyes...

finishText.en:
Rowdies! My darlings! Alive and kicking!
Gosh... I thought I'd never see you again!
Thank you, friend, for helping out!

goal.en: Escort the Rowdy Family and Roman Lazeykin to the docks on Draconid Island.

startText.en:
We fought like lions! Bam - one down! Crushed another! Grabbed the third by the tail and tossed him! The fourth lost a few teeth! The fifth... We smacked him as high as we could reach. Serves him right!
Then we were captured... Jeez... They threatened to eat us! Only they couldn't agree on how - boil, fry, or gut and roast over fire. Awful, just awful! Next time we won't be so easy on the bastards! And we'll be that much smarter about it, too!
Anyway, enough chit-chat. They can spot us and throw us right back into the next empty cage.
Let's get back to Lazeykin. He might be an imperial subject, but he's a good friend who didn't leave us when we needed him!

checkText.en: I hope you've got some good news?

finishText.en:
Acid, you say... Yes, that's possible. Besides, I think it's the only option.
But that doesn't mean I like it! Then again, what can you do? A mission is a mission.

goal.en: Locate a clutch of draconid eggs and find a way to destroy them. Then return to Roman Lazeykin at the dockside of Draconid Island.

startText.en:
Now that the Rowdies are safe, it's time to get to what we've come here for - sabotage!
Listen up. As you remember, there are clutches of draconid eggs here on the island. Something you are partially responsible for, incidentally. Which means you'll also be the one to correct this mistake.
Locate a clutch and find a way to break the eggs. If we succeed, the draconids will have no future. Without new fighters, their defeat in the war will be a matter of time.
Regretfully, neither the Rowdies nor I can assist you on this mission. We've been seriously beaten up in that scuffle. I'll send the Rowdies to the Citadel so that the little ones get some rest, which they badly deserve. I myself will stay here to wait for news from you.
Now go, and don't delay. We have lots and lots to do.

checkText.en: What news do you bring, Keeper of the Revelation?

finishText.en:
Great news! You've rid us of a heavy burden. Now that the draconid threat is eliminated, the Citadel inhabitants will breathe easier.
I'm grateful beyond words. Yet I hope you'll find my gift to your liking.

goal.en: Soften the shells of 5 draconid eggs with acid, break the eggs and report to the Keeper of Power at the Master's Citadel.

startText.en:
That's what they call peace, heh... No, old grudges cannot be forgotten in a matter months. No way they can... A single spark was enough for the flame of animosity to flare up anew.
But perhaps we can take advantage of it. While the wormfaces are fighting the draconids, we'll take them out one at a time. Anyway, that's not for us to worry about. We have our mission.
The clutch needs to be destroyed. Luckily, and in no small part thanks to you and our former wormfaced friends, I now know what needs to be done. If they use acid to destroy draconid egg shells, then we can do the same. You get the idea?
I have a few acid bottles that I had planned to use for a different purpose, but now... It's better to make use of them here.
So grab the bottles and go! Splash some acid on an egg and hit it with all your might. Break five eggs and then we'll see what those scaly beasts will do when left without their offspring! And we'll be there to direct their rage on the wormfaces. Now that's what I call two birds with one stone!

checkText.en: Heh, I'd be glad to get some exercise, but I'm here to gather information. I mustn't die in battle.

name.en: The Good, the Bad and the Dead

startText.en:
Look, with you here and some of the draconids off somewhere in the Misty Lands, we need to take advantage of the situation. What do you say?
Not many draconids stayed here on the island, but they are still a threat to flank us. It would be wise to get rid of that threat.
So let's not waste any time! Go kill as many draconids as you can. The only thing I can say after their betrayal is this: the only good draconid is a dead draconid!

finishText.en:
Howdy, beanpole! Come on in, make yourself at home. The lakefolk are always glad to see you!
Are you here on business or just dropping by for some fish soup?

goal.en: Meet chieftain Smack the Lakefolk at Eldress Lake.

startText.en:
Listen up, soldier! We need to talk.
Here's the deal. Drabova says you're planning to fight a golem? Heh, and they say we orcs are stupid and always trying to solving our problems with brute force... They say we have to use our heads, hah!
Well, now we're at peace with those slimies. They've been living in their puddle for who knows how many decades, and they've seen our wormfaced friends rest... resto... I mean, fix that massive golem!
And if I were you, I'd talk to the slimies' leader before trying to climb the bayonets ass first. Perhaps you'll work out a better idea, eh!

finishText.en: Oh! You're our best friend of all! In our village you'll always find food and shelter. Only you won't find that thing... That thing has been stolen!

startText.en:
I take it you're afraid of the big rattler? Well, you should be! We didn't used to fear it. What's there to fear? A block of stone lying at the bottom of the lake, covered in slit with only its head sticking out?
But then one night I heard a rattle! I went to check it out and saw a swarm of tiny little rattlers. They were all over, making all kinds of noise, toppling the fences and scaring away the fish... I almost had a heart attack! But they didn't react at all. They lined up around the lake and just stood there, waiting. And then one of them stepped forward, holding this strange this, all glowing and iridescent. He pointed it at the lake, and the water erupted with waves, one bigger than the other! Three of my nets were washed away... Brand new ones, too - a real pity! Anyway, I looked at the lake and saw this mass rising up from the center of the lake - a big rattler! I literally froze in fear. Perhaps it had been asleep, not dead, and the small rattler woke him up with that thing before falling asleep himself. The big rattler grabbed the small one and dragged him away. The other rattlers followed suit, leaving the strange thing behind. I picked it up once fear released me. I sensed something about this thing, that it was important... But I won't just give it to you.
Let's trade! I'll give you the thing and you help me out with a small affair. See all those drakes on the cliffs? They've been picking on us, stealing our fish, ruining the nets and setting our houses on fire... I'm so sick of them!
So let's do this: you take care of the drakes for us and I'll give you this thing, whatever it is, OK? You'll find good use for it, I swear by the toad!

checkText.en: Why are you distracting me? Can't you see I'm busy?!

finishText.en: Wait a sec... That's the June golem control mechanism! What a find... Where did you manage to get it?

goal.en: Find the crab that stole the "strange thing" in Eldress Lake and take it back. Then bring the June artifact to Semer Shabas at the Outpost.

startText.en: We don't have the strange thing... I took it with me when I left the house, sat down on the shore and started fixing the net. I put the thing next to me to keep an eye on it. I got distracted with all the knots, and when I looked up I saw a crab crawling by. There's lots of them in the lake, massive ones too. I got all happy, thinking dinner was coming my way. I bent down to grab the harpoon, and that's when I saw the thing in its pincers! I forgot all about the harpoon and started chasing the crab, but... It reached the water in a matter of seconds... I feel terrible, but there's no way I can help you now. We're small and those crabs are huge. I can't defeat the beast in the water. But you're a beanpole, I'm sure you can handle it. Only I don't know which of them got the thing. Hmm...

checkText.en: A very interesting artifact... Perhaps we've actually surpassed the Junes in several fields of technology and magic. That said, we've still got ways to go to compete with them in integrating magical and physical devices into operational mechanisms!

finishText.en: Everything's ready! I removed the unnecessary parts, made a few adjustments and charged it with energy. Now this thing is your ticket out of here. With this device you can easily get to the old portal without disturbing the guardian. Were I you, however, I'd kill him anyway, since it poses a serious threat to all of us. Besides, I'm also curious what he's got on the inside!

goal.en: Get 75 power cells by fighting golems at the Frontier and return to Semer Shabas.

startText.en:
How curious... So, you're saying this artifact helped regular golems raise the huge Guardian from the bottom of the lake? Well, that explains a number of things!
This thing must be a remote control. The ancient Junes were quite militaristic at the dawn of their civilization. They hid war machines in a bunch of secret places to use should the need arise. It appears that the guardian watching the portal is one such reserve machine.
Back then the Junes integrated separate power cells into their golems. After all, the crystals that power golems could be destroyed, while a golem with a built-in power supply could operate without recharging for a long time. When the wormfaces came here, they discovered one of the old hiding places, switched on the old golems and then the Guardian.
As for the artifact you've found, things aren't as simple. As far as I understand, it's broken and quite useless for us at this point. Perhaps it was ruined by water or some internal component is out of order. Could be I'll be able to fix and even modify it to work as a key to the portal and a friendly-or-hostile detector so that the Guardian doesn't attack you. But for that I'll need golem power cells. And lots of them! We'll have to disassemble at least seventy golems to understand their design and fix your "remote".

checkText.en: Well, did you teach those scoundrels a lesson? Even if they all turn to water, I won't shed a single tear, trust me on that!

finishText.en: Aha! That'll teach them how to ruin our nets and scare away the fish! Grr, blasted troglodytes! Serves them right!

startText.en:
As if there wasn't enough to worry about... Did you happen to meet the Riverfolk tribe? They're very much like us, only they're bad. Evil. And the reason they're evil is that their river has dried out.
It used to be different around here: we, the Lakefolk, would fish in the lake and the Riverfolk would fish in the river. Everyone was happy. There was enough food and enough space to satisfy everyone. Then the river started to dry out all of a sudden.
We always got along well with our neighbors! So when they hit hard times we let them have half our lake. Eldress Lake is big and can feed many mouths! But instead...
Our nets are getting torn, our fishing spots ransacked... And now our villagefolk are disappearing. And the Riverfolk don't even want to talk to us and won't let us into their village. My brother went to see them to try and resolve the issue in a neighborly fashion, but he never returned. And now it turns out he's been sitting in a draconid cage all this. Looks like the Riverfolk have been giving our waterfolk away to the draconids! There must be payback... I mean, their behavior is not very neighborly!

checkText.en: We Lakefolk are a peaceful race. Those who come with good intentions are treated with respect. But aggressors get what they deserve. Eldress Lake is big and deep... And the fish don't mind a treat every once in a while.

finishText.en:
I heard screams coming from the other shore of the lake. That must have been the end of that rotten Snap the Riverfolk. Oh, I hope they pick out a decent chieftain, so that we may live in peace like before.
And you, beanpole, have earned the respect of our tribe. Here is your due reward!

goal.en: Kill Snap the Riverfolk, the Riverfolk chieftain, and return to Smack the Lakefolk in the village on Eldress Lake.

startText.en:
I've been thinking... The Riverfolk did not attack us on their own volition. We have lived side by side for many moons! Every spawning season we got together and celebrate. When we'd catch a 350-pound catfish, we always invited them over for a feast. Our relations were friendly, like proper neighbors!
But after the old Plop the Riverfolk died, a new chieftain took over, named Snap. Ever since then there's been no peace between us.
I think that Snap is rotten. He's got a rotten heart, and that rot is spreading through the entire Riverfolk tribe. He's the one turning them against us, no one else would do it. And if you pierce his rotten heart right through, that would put an end to all this animosity between our tribes, and we'd go back to peaceful coexistence, like before. Please, help my race, will you?

checkText.en: Hey, we know you! Keeper of the Revelation... Gosh, we envy you so much!

finishText.en:
When the draconids and the wormfaces quarreled with the Master, we just happened to be here. Working on building the Outpost, yeah. This place was run by the draconids. Drakes, draconids and shamans performed their rituals. They say even the draconid queen, whom they call "mother," dwells here. Though we've never seen her... Just imagine how huge she must be, eh?
But then all hell broke loose! Bang, bang, golems here, draconids there, and massacre all around. Right. Our Outpost turned out to be right on the frontline. With draconids pushing on one side and wormfaces crawling out of subterranean tunnels on the other, we found ourselves smack between a rock and a hard place!

goal.en: Board an astral sloop and go to the Frontier.

startText.en:
Excellent job, Keeper of the Revelation. I knew you'd be able to crush our enemies right in their lair!
But don't let it go to your head! We've won the battle, but not the war. It turns out that our enemies have settled on an island named the Frontier.
Judging by the scouts' reports the draconids and the wormfaces were unable to overcome their thousand-year animosity after all, and have resumed their fighting once more. I'm sure you realize that this is to our advantage.
Regretfully, there aren't that many Attendants here in the Citadel who are ready to fight. This is why we've hired mercenaries: orcs, humans, elves, gibberlings and others who stay true to the Master's Word. I hope you'll be able to cooperate with them, so that together you'll crush the vile traitors.
Now go. Board an astral sloop and be on your way. May the Master's Will protect you!

checkText.en: I think I understand now how to track down the wormfaces who are operating the golems. But it's still too early to talk details.

finishText.en: Cool, now I have a rough sketch. Now let me try something...

startText.en:
I fear the draconids will prove useless. If their chieftain knows nothing, the rest of them know even less. They're absolutely brainless.
We need to capture and interrogate a wormface. A draconid told me that the wormfaces are hiding underground and controlling the golems remotely. But how can we get them underground? I'm no gopher...
Wait a sec, I have an idea. A golem can't be controlled directly as it's not alive. This means the wormfaces are using some kind of a remote control device. If we capture such a device and study it, we'll find out where the signal is coming from.
Will you do it? All you need to do is break apart a few golems and bring me all the parts that at least vaguely resemble a transmitter. In the meantime I'll think about how to make a device that will help us find the wormface.

checkText.en: Light, blasted light! I've gone blind!

finishText.en: What on earth do you want from me?! Ask, I'll tell you all I know... Argh, cursed light! It's burning!

goal.en: Use the locator to find the hiding wormface, use a thunderstone to make him come out and interrogate him.

startText.en:
All right, so this wire goes here... The gear goes there. Tighten the screws. Close the circuit... Let's check it... There's a signal! Hurray!
I really didn't expect it to be so easy. I must admit that wormfaces have fantastic technology. Anyway, I managed to modify the golem's receiver into a primitive locator. From now on the device will emit a shrill squealing sound in response to the control signal that comes from the wormface operating the golem. The closer the wormface, the louder the squealing will be!
All you need to do is find the spot where the squealing is especially loud. That will be the spot where the wormface is hiding underground.
Remember the thunderstones? I have some here. Oh, I also tinkered with them when I had some free time... Anyway, they're now a bit louder than normal stones... I'd say three times as loud, hehe. I don't have a lot of them, but I can spare you for your cause. If you detonate this stone above the wormface's head, he will pop out of the ground like a cork out of a bottle. Ready to repent for all sins, even those he didn't commit. I'm telling you this as an agent! Whose agent? Umm... Nobody's agent, I work for myself. Now go and don't fill your head with needless ideas. You'll be safer that way!

checkText.en: Well, have you learned anything interesting?

finishText.en: That does sound interesting...

goal.en: Relay the information obtained from the wormface to Larisa Dymkina.

startText.en:
Damn it! You loyal underlings of Nihaz don't understand a thing. All the lies have poisoned your minds! And this blind faith will lead you to your graves!
Long ago our race believed Nihaz. And what became of us? Worthless, pathetic creatures living underground! Argh... The cursed sun is burning my eyes!
Sarn, the mad Sarn had cast a Curse that almost killed us all. Those who survived ran to Nihaz in fear. They prayed for salvation, pleading for protection against the Curse. He laughed and turned the surviving Junes into wormfaces. Aye, we changed and the June Curse disappeared. We kept our lives... But can this be called life?! Eternal wretched existence in the dark, eternal fear, eternal anguish and boredom...
We hate Nihaz, and our hatred is centuries old. And now is our chance to exact vengeance! On a small shard east of the Frontier there's a teleport that's been preserved by sheer luck. It can let through an entire army! We'll infiltrate the Dead City, crushing everything in our path, and capture that which will grant us redemption. Let the gods continue their wars. And we'll depart for a place where no one will disturb us. This miserable world can continue its prolonged agony. We don't give a damn!

checkText.en: Freeze, panic! Who you be?

finishText.en:
You say the fuzzies sent you? What fuzzies? Oh, the Watchful Family! That's what I call them, hehe. Don't worry, I'm not one to pay a creature's skin color any mind. As long as you're a good fighter, everything else is unimportant.
The entrance to the wormface cave is to the north. That's bad, very bad. We're talking literally a stone's throw from the Outpost.
And the draconids have an altar in the ruins that's teeming with their priests? And they're keeping the slimies caged? Oh, that's a bad sign. Wherever magic is involved, it's wise to expect ill things. Better smash their heads in with your fist before they use it, hehe!

goal.en: Inspect the terrain around the Outpost and report the recon results to Outpost commander Gammon the Tempestuous.

startText.en:
Enemies everywhere! Sprang up as if out of the ground... Well, at least the wormfaces did, literally. And we don't even know the tac... tas... damn it. Forgot the word!
Anyway, we need to scout the area and see who's where. What if the enemies are hiding something interesting? And we don't know it! That won't fly! We're scouts, after all, and we must know everything.
Only we can't leave this place. We need to meet up with other fighters to explain to them the tac... tas... tactical situation, there! Explain the tactical situation!
Good thing you were sent to our aid. Help us, will you? All you need is to carefully inspect the terrain around the Outpost. Our kind is few in number at the Outpost, so we have no one to send out on patrol. What if the enemies are scheming up to attack? Forewarned is forearmed. That's what mothers told us since we were babies!

checkText.en: Hey, fighter, where do you come from? I haven't seen you around here before. What if you're a spy, eh?

finishText.en: Wow. You say Cake sent you here? And kicked some draconid butt along the way? That's the way we do it! I came, I saw, I smashed to pieces! Keep it up, soldier! I'm grateful to you, hehe!

goal.en: Destroy the draconids' altar in the Tuk-Miktu Ruins and report to Gammon the Tempestuous at the Outpost upon completion.

startText.en:
Look, I had this idea... Yeah, I can think too, imagine that! Pay no mind to my size and stupid-looking mug. If anything, that's my mom's fault. Well, I like me some grub, too, just like any other orc. But my brain still works like a well-oiled machine, believe that! Anyway, what was I talking about...
Right! It's time we tan the draconids' hides some. I'm sick and tired of them! Those scaly bastards have entrenched themselves in the ruins to the east, working their vile magics undisturbed. They built an altar and snatched up a bunch of slimies. Been guarding them like hawks, too! The little ones... I'm talking about the Watchfulls... They were on a recon mission and barely managed to save their furry butts! And that road is how we get our reinforcements. I bet my tooth it's no accident that the scaly bastards are working their sorcery there! They're scheming up something dirty and devious!
Go to the Tuk-Miktu Ruins and wreak some havoc! Smash the altar to bits, and make the draconids choke with anger! Well, how do you like that plan? Hehe.
And when you're done, go to the Outpost and report to our superior. His name's Gammon the Tempestuous. Tell him Cake is carrying out his duties perfectly, keeps alert when standing guard and all that good stuff. Your reward won't be long in coming either, hehe!

checkText.en: What do you want in our village, beanpole?! Get lost! This is our water. Our soil. And the fish in the lake is all ours, too!

finishText.en:
What? My brother's alive? Thank the gods! I was sure he'd turned to water by now...
Consider yourself the best friend of all the Lakefolk! I give you my word, and my word is stronger than ice!

goal.en: Release the captured waterfolk in the Tuk-Miktu Ruins and report the rescue to chieftain Smack the Lakefolk.

startText.en:
Look... Here's the deal. We're trying to come to an agreement with the slimies that live by the lake. Like, we give them glass beads and they give us... Nope, not gold. What the hell do we need gold for?! We're running out of grub to eat, and you can't eat gold!
So, we want to make a deal with their leader. We want to trade! Exchange trinkets for grub like fish and crawfish... Only those Lakefolk are stubborn like damn trolls. They refuse to deal outright! We don't want nothing fancy either. Hunger's a real bitch, we're willing to settle for the basics but they still won't budge!
So here's what I think. The Watchfulls report that some of the captured waterfolk are being kept in the ruins. If you release them, the waterfolk leader might be willing to compromise. Well, do you think it will work?

finishText.en: Looks like our reinforcements have arrived! What took you so long? What, you say you weren't receiving my reports?! Ugh, I wouldn't put it past that twit to wipe his ass with them!

goal.en: Meet with saboteur Larisa Dymkina, who is hiding somewhere near the Smoldering Highland.

startText.en:
Listen up. There was a female hanging around here. A sharp cookie, and quick in all kinds of ways. You could see right away she's a saboteur, but doesn't seem to be from the committee. A damn fine woman, if only she weren't so small, hehe!
Anyway, I sent her out on a recon mission. Those Imperial saboteurs are trained specifically for these jobs. But for some reason I've had no reports from her in a long time. What if something's happened to her? I'm already short of people with no one to send out on a search mission. And so I'm forced to turn to freelancers like you.
The saboteur's name's Larisa Dymkina. In her last report she said she was going somewhere near the Smoldering Highland. Find her, will you? She might need help or something.

checkText.en: You evil! Me gives up!

finishText.en: Me not tells you a thing! Not tells... Not tells... Tells... Tells? Tells! Me tells all things! Your asks... Asks... Me talks...

goal.en: Lure Broga, the draconid chieftain, into an ambush by Larisa Dymkina. Once Broga is exhausted from the fight, inject him with the truth serum and interrogate him thoroughly.

startText.en:
OK, what's done is done. One's as good as none, but two are a squad. Moreover, I have a plan. What plan? Very simple.
We still can't understand what the draconids and the wormfaces are doing here and why they're fighting each other. And if anyone can shed some light on the matter, it's surely the draconids themselves! You dig?
So, I caught a glimpse of a draconid in the ruins on the Smoldering Highland. It was either a chieftain or a shaman - I couldn't say for sure. You know them better. And that is why this job is for you.
The plan is this: we need to lure the chieftain into an ambush and interrogate him. The problem is he's almost invulnerable in his lair. I don't know how, but he always keeps a protective spell on himself, and that's something I know a lot about. But if we lure him out of the camp and into an ambush, I'll be able to dispel his magic. And then all we have to do is inject him with truth serum, and he'll start talking like nobody's business. In the committee we... Oops! I didn't say that, understand?
Here is the truth serum from my personal supplies. Don't ask me where I got it. Lure the draconid chieftain into my ambush. We'll tire him out by fighting and then you'll inject him with the serum. He'll soften up some, and that's when we'll get all the truth out of him.

finishText.en: So that's it... Turns out their Fiery Father knew everything beforehand. And the betrayal was carefully planned. And the only reason the Fiery Father has entered into an alliance with the Master was to gain access... To what? It'd be great if we could find out more about that.

goal.en: Discuss the information obtained from Broga with saboteur Larisa Dymkina.

startText.en:
Fiery Father talk to ours... Order to whack worms-on-faces... Worms-on-faces be enemy. Become friend. Now again enemy. Our fights!
Worms-on-faces fights cowardly! They sits under the ground. Operates golem! Golem go, ours fight. Fight strong! But ours not give in. Ours breaks golem. Search worms-on-faces. Search under the grounds! When they goes out, pull them out and whack! And then yum! That's it. Worms-on-faces few. Golem many! But golem can't be yum. Ours try... Tooth crack, crack. Now our tooth hurt...
Fiery Father say if all worms-on-faces dies, only ours stay. Ours go to City on Bones. Ours seek strange thing! Strange thing save ours. World crack! Boom! Ours stay safe. Ours go far away and stay safe. Other burns. Fiery Father say so!

checkText.en: A draconid is just a big lizard. I wonder why they don't shed their tails when in danger?

finishText.en:
Aha! Take that, you scaly scum! Leave us alone!
Thank you so much, pal! I don't know what we'd do without you.

startText.en:
Hey, soldier! Why are you hanging around here? Got nothing to do?
I'll find a task for you, no problem! We're few in number, so every blade is a blessing.
Recently the draconids have increased their raids on the Outpost. We've been holding our ground so far, but each attack takes a toll and I don't know how long we can go on. So, please do me a favor and give the draconids hell! I want them to forget the way to this place!

checkText.en: It's a pity golems can't be re-subdued to our will. They would make perfect fighters, what with their great strength and stamina, no need for food, never falling asleep at the post, never getting hammered at some tavern...

finishText.en: The golem commander is no more? Excellent! Thank you so much!

goal.en: Participate in killing the wormface dominator and return to Agatha Grekhova at the Outpost.

startText.en:
We're sick and tired of those golems! Not that they pose a real threat... But they're getting more organized by the day!
I think that whichever wormface is operating the golems have picked our camp as a training ground. That doesn't make me happy at all, and that's putting it lightly.
Will you help us? The scum operating the golems ought to have his facial tentacles tied around his ass! I think he's hiding somewhere north of the Outpost. But to lure him out from under ground where those cowards usually hide, you'll need a thunderstone. Toss it inside the hiding place and the tentacle-faced bastard will bolt out at once!
And be sure to take some friends with you! I have a feeling that wormface will prove tougher than others.

checkText.en: After such boorish behavior, I wouldn't give a dented penny to save Grosh's life!

finishText.en:
That's it! Thank you, friend!
Now, those friggin' lizards will think twice before showing such vulgar things to an honest girl!

goal.en: Participate in killing Grosh, the draconid leader, and return to Agatha Grekhova at the Outpost.

startText.en:
Gosh, am I angry! This draconid named Grosh is apparently quite the joker. What a bastard!
Every night he gets on top of a hill and starts flashing me all kinds of indecent gestures! And more than just gestures... I'm going to... I'll... I'd strangle the bastard with my bare hands for such insinuations!
Only I can't leave the camp. And that bastard is obviously mocking me on purpose. Once my fighters and I set out to beat his skull in, but apparently there's a whole squad of them behind the hill... A real trickster, that one!
How would you like to defend a maiden's honor? Find Grosh and smash his mug in so he can't even walk. But beware - he's a tough cookie! You shouldn't go after him by yourself. Big bastards like him should be taken on with a group, just in case.

finishText.en:
Goodness gracious... I couldn't dream that you'd handle war machines that were designed to kill with such ease.
 This clearly shows that mind is superior to technology!

kickText.en: You know, looking at an attacking golem you'd never think all it is, is clay, sand, iron and some magic.

checkText.en: Alpha chromosome, beta chromosome, genetic changes, mutation... No, that's not what I need!

finishText.en: Hrm. Was the patient struck on the head with a heavy object? Was the specimen extracted carefully and without injury? Listen, I know your idea of "anesthesia": smack the patient's head with a club, and there you go.

goal.en: Get a wormface's brain, use the transmitter to summon Sarbaz Gurguf, give him the brain and receive further instructions.

startText.en:
Wait, don't distract me. I'm thinking... Thinking... Thinking... Damn it, you distracted me!
What do you want? Just saying hi? What impudence! I was one step away from a spectacular discovery. Now I've lost my train of thought because of you!
All right, listen, now that I'm distracted, you might as well make yourself useful.
I'm researching psionic capabilities of those you call "wormfaces." Their true name is far more complicated, you wouldn't even be able to pronounce half of it.
Now, do you know that wormfaces can have tremendous influence on your mind? That's right. I want to understand where they get that power and how it is generated...
I need their brain! Fresh and intact. I sense that it conceals lots of mysteries.
What's in it for you? How about fame and respect of the entire scientific community?!
However, I need an absolutely fresh brain! While you carry it around in your backpack, all the neural connections will be lost. This is why I'm giving you the transmitter. When you get the brain, press the big red button. Then, guided by the signal, I'll be able to get to you under cover of invisibility. I hope the wormfaces won't spot me... I'd do anything for the sake of science!

checkText.en: I wonder if the Keepers have developed naturally or were bred Perhaps they hold the same status as the termite queen?

finishText.en:
Is this a brain? It is. One unit. Looks like a normal brain.
Strange... It's not quite normal! Look, there's a strange spot here near the hypothalamus...
Wait, you mean that's dirt from your grimy hands?! Oh, astral demons take me! You don't handle valuable research materials in this fashion!

goal.en: Get a Keeper's brain, use the transmitter to summon Sarbaz Gurguf, give him the brain and receive further instructions.

startText.en:
Interesting... Wait a minute, let me think.
If they have unstable connections, that means... What about the cause for the development of stable psionic heredity? No, no, that's not it at all!
Listen. The brains I have are no good. I can't understand what the secret is.
You'll have to continue searching and get me new materials to study. I reckon a Keeper's brain would be useful. I trust you have a thunderstone with you? Without it you won't have a chance going up against a Keeper.
When you're done, use the transmitter and hand over the research material to me.

checkText.en: Did you manage to get the brain I need? Science can't wait!

finishText.en:
Wow! That is something... This is the first time I see a brain so complicated and highly developed!
I bet that the creature this brain belonged to used much more than just 10 percent of it... I could have been 100, maybe even 120! I sincerely regret its death, but science demands sacrifice!
OK, I'm heading back to my lab to start studying it.
And you ought to get a reward for your contribution to science. Take your pick!

goal.en: Get a Samum's brain, use the transmitter to summon Sarbaz Gurguf, give him the brain and receive further instructions.

startText.en:
So, the first sample of the wormface's cerebrum is useless and the second one is ruined. What can we do? Here's what we'll do.
I heard from Kirill Pryatkin that he'd met a unique wormface in the depths of the cave. Kirill is a sly fellow and shifty as a rat, and even he barely managed to survive.
Wouldn't it be great to acquire the cerebrum of this monster? Just think how it would aid our research! But don't go charging into battle just yet or he will turn your brains to jelly before you can say your prayers. My scientific experience suggests that this wormface is a serious enemy. You had better gather all of your friends before attempting to sever the wormface from his cerebrum.
But don't delay either, for I'm all feverish with anticipation of the mysteries it may reveal! We're talking a guaranteed new scientific degree! Use the transmitter as soon as you are done. And remember that every minute of my time is precious.

finishText.en:
Ah, so you're the "greatest hero of the past, present and future," as my colleague described you? Odd, you don't look too formidable at all.
But I guess that's all right. I'm currently involved in conducting fascinating scientific research and could use all the help I can get.

goal.en: Meet Yaver Tul at the excavations near the Hissing Canyon.

startText.en:
Wait up! I was requested to give you a message.
Yaver Tul, our best technician, asked someone resembling a battle-hardened hero to meet her in the excavations area. She needs a tight-lipped and quick-witted assistant who could hold their own. And you fit the bill just right!
Yaver Tul is a genius when it comes to war mechanisms. Her hands are made of gold! Well, they look ordinary prosthetics on the outside, but the internal circuits are golden! Trust me, that makes a big difference.
If you prove useful to her, Yaver Tul will reward you generously. So go on, get to the excavations.

checkText.en: Well, how are the crawlers doing? Still breathing? I hope you will fix that soon.

finishText.en:
Wow! That's really strong! A shield like this is truly priceless!
And the mandibles are full of potent acid. One drop will eat through a breastplate. It's just what I needed!

startText.en:
I'm Yaver Tul and I'm conducting research on military applications. And presently I'm in dire need of a hero like you.
I've been told there are massive gars in the Hissing Canyon. Their mandibles look so formidable that I wouldn't risk coming close to them for the all treasures in the Universe!
But you aren't afraid of some ugly bugs, are you?
The point is that the crawlers' mandibles contain a special thick liquid. Incidentally, it's almost an ideal solvent, though that's irrelevant.
The gars' plates are very light, sturdy, flexible, and tough as a sheet of steel! It's a pity I have only a few samples. If I want to perform more serious research, I will obviously need more. I know that if I had more shields, I could invent a brand new type of armor!

checkText.en: If I could make armor out of Rocktooth's breastplate, it will be a genuine masterpiece!

finishText.en:
Wow! Now that's a plate! How did you manage to best a creature with such a thick hide? Then again, I don't particularly care about that. The important thing is that you did it, and in doing so you've earned this reward.
Now I'm going to start tinkering with fittings. Who knows, perhaps soon all military weapons and armor will bear my brand!

goal.en: Participate in killing Rocktooth and bring its breastplate to Yaver Tul at the researchers' camp by the entrance to the wormface cave.

startText.en:
I can only make light armor out the plates I have. Tough as they are, they are still far too fragile for a heavy breastplate. A few strong blows would be enough to crack them.
I need something stronger... Like the plates of a very mature gar.
I saw one like it in the depths of the Hissing Canyon. A horrible beast! I don't think you can kill him on your own. But if you're not alone... So gather your friends and go. Bring me its breastplate! My reward will be generous.

finishText.en: Hey, you! Psst... Come here. Be quiet, those tentacle-faced beasts have keen hearing.

goal.en: Meet with Kirill Pryatkin in the wormface cave on the Island of Revelation.

startText.en:
Keeper of the Revelation! Don't be surprised - now that you know the Truth, this title is rightfully yours. I have an important errand for you.
You already know that wormfaces have betrayed us and the Master. Well, in doing so they have also signed their own death warrant. Their actions have effectively nullified all rules and agreements that were in effect. Including the agreement restricting surface inhabitants from going down into their cave.
A seasoned scout named Kirill Pryatkin was sent down there, but I'm afraid there's no way he can do the job all alone.
Go into the wormface cave and locate Kirill, and the two of you can decide on the best course of action. The more damage you cause to the enemy now, the less trouble they'll be to us later.

checkText.en: Well, did you find anything valuable?

finishText.en: This is quite an unusual stone. I've seen its kind before. Remember the "kaboomers" that were used to blow up demonic portals on the Twilight Isle? Well, kaboomers are actually made out of plain-looking stones like this one. The draconids call them thunderstones. When thrown they explode with a super-bright flare. And it appears that the flare blinds the Keepers, so that they become completely defenseless. Interesting, yes? And certainly useful.

goal.en: Search the draconid remains and take everything that might be used to destroy the Keepers, then report your findings to Kirill Pryatkin.

startText.en:
I heard about you from my sister. Do your remember her? She says your help at the Dragon Ring proved quite useful. I trust my sister and therefore I trust you.
Now listen carefully. There aren't that many wormfaces left here in the cave. Most of them have gone off somewhere deep into the Misty Lands. The ones who stayed behind are mainly scientists, researchers and Keepers. And I want to talk to you about the Keepers.
They differ considerably from regular wormfaces. Not only are they taller and considerably stronger, their greatest distinction is their magic. They can boil your brains right inside your head!
And yet I've seen draconids sneak into the cave and kill Keepers outright. Granted, they didn't survive themselves, but it's interesting to note that Keepers can, in fact, be killed. No, not "can be" - must be!
Look around. Perhaps you'll be able to find out how the draconids managed to wipe out so many wormfaces. If I were you, I would start by searching the bodies of the dead draconids and the nearby items. I'll be right behind you. But don't expect me to help in combat - I am a scout, not a warrior. If I could cut through enemies by the dozen, I'd do it without you.

checkText.en: I saw an explosion in the depths of the cave and heard sounds of battle. Is the Keeper dead?

finishText.en:
Hehehe, I bet the Keeper can now be swept into a dustpan and kept in a fist-size box, right? Great!
And he had this bottle with acid on him? Don't be in a rush to thrash it. I reckon we can use any information, technology, weapons and materials used by wormfaces in this war.

goal.en: Destroy a Keeper using a thunderstone, and signal Kirill Pryatkin with the signal lamp.

startText.en:
These days it's the Keepers that pose the greatest threat to us. If you kill enough Keepers, other wormfaces will be disorganized and won't put up much of a resistance. But there's a problem: killing a Keeper is far from easy.
However, there's a way. This thunderstone here. Its flare can literally burn the Keeper's eyes out, since they're only used to subterranean darkness. And then you should have no trouble killing him!
I'll give you a signal lamp. It has a very narrow beam that can hardly be seen from a distance. If you need me, give me a signal by flashing the light three times

checkText.en: I heard explosions in the depths of the cave. Are the Keepers dead?

finishText.en:
Hehehe, judging by the racket, I bet the Keeper can now be swept into a dustpan and kept in a fist-size box, right? Great!
And the acid on them may just prove useful. Don't be in a rush to thrash it.

That's really great news! While there's discord and friction among the wormfaces, they pose no threat to us.
Now we ought to shift out focus to draconids. If we deal with them, half of our problems will be solved!

goal.en: Report on the elimination of the wormface threat to the Keeper of Power at the Master's Citadel.

startText.en:
You've won a glorious victory today, my friend! I'm certain that the Keeper's death has had great impact on all wormfaces. And I'm even more certain that the cave inhabitants will have other things besides us to worry about in the near future.
Go to the Citadel and report to the Keeper of Power this delightful news! And take care of yourself. The wormfaces may be down, but they're not out. And after a while they'll surely be a nuisance again. So be sure to drop by later. I'll brief you on the current events, and together we'll think of more ways to frustrate our enemies.

checkText.en: They're disgusting, those wormfaces. It's obvious that we won't come to an agreement. Why did we even bother?

startText.en:
They are way too many of those tentacle-faced freakshows for my liking... And with their excellent engineering and psionic abilities, they can wreak enormous damage should they decide to attack the Citadel. Ugh, how I hate fighting on three fronts! Wormfaces on one side, draconids on the other, all the while demons and cultists are operating their own island.
Well, what we can do is focus on eliminating at least one threat, and that's the wormfaces. They're so afraid of death you'd think they're planning to live forever. If we kill a score of them, the others will simmer down in no time!

checkText.en: Hey, soldier, you don't look so good! Just out of combat, eh?

finishText.en: So you gave the draconids in the ruins a good beating? That's good, hehe! I'd challenge them myself, but who's gong to stay in command? No, I can't leave the post! I need to maintain discipline and cultivate productivity among my subordinates. Everything is pursuant to regulations!

startText.en:
You're taking the old road through the ruins to get to the Outpost, right? Then keep your eyes open! A whole gang of draconids has settled there! They're as wicked as Cake when he gets hung over. Their teeth are this big! We barely managed to escape them.
We were using the road to deliver provisions, but now that those bastards are there we have no choice but to transport everything by water. The lake is wet and dangerous, and you feel like the boat will overturn at any moment...
So, listen, we need a favor. Beat the snot out of the draconids when you run into them. Damn goons shouldn't be lusting after our supplies. If you do it, all of our soldiers will be mighty grateful!

checkText.en: Hey? What do you want? Bugs? What friggin' bugs? Are you high? I don't know nothin' about no bugs!

finishText.en:
Is that right... So now we can see half the island in detail without having to raise our asses off the stool? Whoa, the Watchfulls sure are something else! Granted, they deserve an undressing for their... whatchamacallit... ill-advised initiative! But seeing as things worked out so well with the bugs and the squinteyes , I will instead thank you both!
I wonder what would happen if you planted such a bug in a ladies' bathhouse? Hey, that's not a bad idea!
This draconid was unlucky... He looks as though he was trampled by a squad of war rhinos.

goal.en: Go to the Tuk-Miktu Ruins and find out the location of the recent battle.

startText.en:
Listen up. Last night, I decided to take a leak outside the Outpost's perimeter. Sometimes you just need some privacy, you know? So anyway, I was just standing there, bothering no one. The breeze was pleasant, the crickets were singing, the creek was bubbling... It was paradise!
And then came a huge explosion over the Tuk-Miktu Ruins to the south! Kaboom! I couldn't help but duck and cover! And then I heard sounds of a vicious battle coming from that direction. The wind carried much of the sounds loud and clear. Draconids shouting, fireballs raging, and some kind of round and blazing thing swishing through the air. The racket lasted for a few minutes and then died down just as suddenly.
I wanted to send my scouts there, but they're all already standing their watch. You're my only hope! Go there quietly and find out what happened. But watch your back. There are more draconids in there than my grandpa has war medals!

finishText.en: This draconid was unlucky... He looks as though he was trampled by a squad of war rhinos.

goal.en: Go to the Tuk-Miktu Ruins and find out the location of the recent battle.

startText.en:
Listen up. Last night, I decided to take a leak outside the Outpost's perimeter. Sometimes you just need some privacy, you know? So anyway, I was just standing there, bothering no one. The breeze was pleasant, the crickets were singing, the creek was bubbling... It was paradise!
And then came a huge explosion over the Tuk-Miktu Ruins to the south! Kaboom! I couldn't help but duck and cover! And then I heard sounds of a vicious battle coming from that direction. The wind carried much of the sounds loud and clear. Draconids shouting, fireballs raging, and some kind of round and blazing thing swishing through the air. The racket lasted for a few minutes and then died down just as suddenly.
I wanted to send my scouts there, but they're all already standing their watch. You're my only hope! Go there quietly and find out what happened. But watch your back. There are more draconids in there than my grandpa has war medals!

checkText.en: I... knew... I cannot... beat... you...

finishText.en:
Dying at the hand of... The strongest... is no shame...
There's great... power... behind you... It's generous to those... who... can understand... its... essence..
You... call it... a Patron... That is incorrect... With time... you'll understand...
Pay me one last... honor... Take my mask... Let this... be... your... trophy...
Fa... farewell...

goal.en: Follow the strange bloody tracks to find the draconid's killer.

startText.en:
The draconid's body is torn to pieces, and it looks as if death came quite recently. The nature of the injuries is unsettling - never before have you seen a weapon that could inflict such horrible wounds. It looks almost as if someone tried to skewer the draconid alive.
To his credit, the draconid put up a desperate resistance. Suddenly you notice strange tracks. Looks like the battle took place elsewhere. The dying draconid managed to grab hold of his enemy and was dragged a few meters. Lightly phosphorescent liquid stains appear to be leading toward the demolished tower to the north. You should follow the tracks to find out which creature attacked the draconid. Perhaps the creature could become an ally?

checkText.en: Why are you disturbing me? Can't you see I'm busy?

finishText.en:
Hrm... So it was a kind of wormface you've never seen before, and he materialized out of thin air? He said something about the Patrons and gave you his mask as a trophy? Interesting, very interesting...
We've already had a few encounters with the creatures you've described. Oh, they are formidable warriors, indeed! Silent, inconspicuous and extremely dangerous! And every of them opted to blow himself up rather than be captured. You're damn lucky that one of these Destroyers deigned to even speak to you. But since he did, perhaps that means you could also master their weapon? We've captured a few trophies, but the weapons all have some strange magic placed on them. They're no more dangerous in the hands of our warriors than a toothpick, though the Destroyers used them to exterminate a whole squad of draconids right in front of our scouts in mere seconds.
But you should go see our expert armorer Yaver Arafi if you want to know more about this weapon. Now go and leave me be. I need to think.

goal.en: Show the Destroyer's Mask to Semer Shabas at the Outpost.

startText.en:
What an interesting mask! You haven't seen anything like this technology even in the wormface cave on the Island of Revelation. Its metal is unbelievably light and extremely tough, and it is entirely unknown to you, though it bears some resemblance to blued steel. And inside the mask you're looking at extremely fine mechanisms...
Perhaps you should show this mask to Semer Shabas. After all, who else but a Zem scientist could make sense of alien technology?

checkText.en: This weapon is probably the strangest thing I've seen in my long lifetime, both before and after death.

finishText.en: Hrm. So the spear that skewered the draconid as if it'd been a duck didn't even graze the golem? Looks like my theory is being confirmed.

goal.en: Test the Destroyer's spear on a draconid and on a golem, then report the results to Yaver Arafi at the Outpost.

startText.en:
I'll give you one of our trophies. Four of our best soldiers and a fellow researcher have perished to acquire this spear. When our fighters finally managed to disarm the wormface, the spear turned into a harmless metal pole! But I saw with my own eyes the Destroyer run that spear through steel armor as if it were a sheet of parchment.
Take the spear and test it... Say, on a golem and on a draconid. You see, I have a theory that the spear is "tuned" to fight certain types of enemies. And if my theory is true...
But it's too early to draw conclusions just yet. First we need to know the result, whatever it is.

checkText.en: I hope you won't chop off your fingers or your head with this chakram.

finishText.en: I was right! The weapon cuts through draconids with ease yet it's totally useless against golems. I guess the saying is true: "dog does not eat dog."

goal.en: Test the Destroyer's chakram on a draconid and on a golem, then report results to Yaver Arafi at the Outpost.

startText.en: And here is another trophy, a throwing disk that belonged to one of the Destroyers. This is a very rare weapon that requires exceptional skill to handle. These disks are called chakram. Its distinctive feature lies in always returning to its owner after it is thrown. We're very lucky to have gotten hold of this chakram. Of course, the actual soldier who had "gotten hold" of it wasn't so lucky... Take this chakram and test it on draconids and golems. I wonder how the weapon will react.

checkText.en: Well, how are you feeling?

finishText.en: Well, well, well... My theory is confirmed. The mask is obviously made to easily operate on the surface both during the day and at night. Wormfaces have very sensitive eyes that cannot bear sunlight. The mask allows them to see in a different spectrum, to feel the creatures' body heat or magic auras. And I bet this mask allows its wearer to see through the veil of invisibility that conceals Destroyers! So there's one use for your trophy. Do you follow?

goal.en: Equip the Destroyer's mask and tell Yaver Arafi what you feel.

startText.en:
The last thing we must do is test the mask itself. Frankly, I am... scared. I don't even know what metal it is made of, never mind all the other questions. I have absolutely no clue what might happen if you put it on. I only hope you won't turn into a Destroyer yourself. Hah!
Anyway, I don't think the Destroyer gave you his mask to kill you. So come on! Equip the mask and tell me what you feel.

checkText.en: I hope you're not distracting me out of idle curiosity?

finishText.en: Ah, I was right! The Destroyers did not harm you! And you say they actually invited you to meet their elder and undergo a trial by combat? Holy cow...

goal.en: Find the Destroyers and return to Semer Shabas at the Outpost. You should search in the vicinities of the Rotten Creek, the Tuk-Miktu Ruins and the Ancient Portal.

startText.en:
Oh yes, I've already heard of your feats and Yaver Arafi's theory. And I agree with him. There's only one thing I don't understand...
Look, we found out that these "Destroyers" are purposefully exterminating draconids. Judging by their considerable progress, they've been warring for over a decade. This raises a question: What did the Destroyer see in you to give you his mask? Perhaps it's because you've won the trust of both the draconids and the wormfaces. You've even managed to stop their endless war for a while... I don't know. But I want to know as much as you do!
And your trophy will help us. Equip the mask, switch on thermal vision and go seek out the Destroyers. They're not going to attack you... At least I hope they won't. I think they're drawn to the ancient ruins. Look for their tracks near the Rotten Creek, the Tuk-Miktu Ruins and the Ancient Portal.

checkText.en: What do you want, hunter?

finishText.en:
You've defeated each of my younger brothers. Truly, that is a heroic feat. I never thought it was possible...
The power that your people call "Patron" has imparted onto you a generous portion of its own might. But I also sense something that my eyes cannot quite see...

goal.en: Meet the Destroyers' Leader in the Dusty Ruins and defeat all Destroyer contenders.

startText.en:
A duel... Well, I don't doubt your abilities. You have enough power to best any enemy. But is it in you to comprehend the kind of power that stands behind the Destroyers? Or the source of their strange magic? Or what the hell they even are?! Well, let's hope your mind is as sharp as your blade.
Go to the Dusty Ruins and show these Destroyers that they're not the only good fighters around!

finishText.en:
I... We... This is... I just don't know what to say! This is incredible! It just cannot be! Look, I already know that the wormfaces used to be Junes. Still, our Patrons are our Patrons! Why would they endow their powers to some underground worms? Besides, if this Kaid character is to be trusted, their powers are radically different from ours. This is very strange...
Either this wormface is a brilliant actor, capable of deceiving even the Purgatory goblin, or everything we know about the Patrons is wrong! But that means the records, the legends... Not to mention our scientific theses and laboratory research studies! I simply cannot fathom it... This is some food for thought, indeed. And I hope you manage to crack the mystery.

goal.en: Return to the Outpost and tell Semer Shabas about what you have seen.

startText.en:
Listen to me, stranger, for I, Kaid, never waste time. Do you think we met by chance? No. Fate itself brought you here. Fate and what you surface dwellers call a "patron." I feel the power brimming within both you and me! And this power comes from the same source.
But my race does not believe in any "patrons"! I chanced to hear about some of your sorcerers who died ages ago. It is said that their Sparks had dissolved in the astral and became what people now call "Patrons." But look at me! My brothers and I are endowed with the same power as you. The fact that you mastered our weapons only proves this. Now think, why would spellcasters from the surface endow underground creatures like us with what appears to be their own power? Why so silent? You don't know what to say? I don't either...
All I know is that there is a mystical power in our world. We call this power the Source. You call it Patrons. Our Source has twelve manifestations, twelve faces. You have twelve Patrons. This power gives you the ability to heal yourself, fight pain and fear, become stronger or more accurate... We cannot do these things. But with the same power we can become invisible, see what is hidden and feel what is concealed... and many things that the surface creatures couldn't even begin to fathom.
Don't let my frankness surprise you. The power of the Source has brought you here, and chose me to be the conductor of its will. I told you much of what we know. Not everything, but quite a lot! Consider it my gift to you for your valor in combat. And now we must part. Remember that our races are enemies. Should fate reunite us on the battlefield, I will not hesitate to kill you, nor will I regret it.
